script: Landlord's Revenge On Me. My family has been renting a house since July 2024. We signed up through a property‑management crew. About a year ago the licensed broker, who ran the company, died, so the house owner took the reins. He's an airline captain, always jet‑setting, but he still came over to chat, signed a fresh lease, and we started doing little projects together. For every tweak he let us in, he'd slash the rent that month. (I am basically a landlord's bestie now.) Fast‑forward to early April. He's out of work, waiting on medical reviews. I, being the genius I am, thought April Fool's would be a blast: "Yo, we're kind of short on rent this month." I didn't even think about his cash flow. He texts back, "Got it, bruh. Pay that balance ASAP." I was like, "Sorry, it's just a prank, we got the cash. Sending it today. Also, I forgot you're short on money." He replied, "I thought it was funny, after the fact, but payback will be coming." (The audacity, bestie.) Mid‑April, we're planning a cruise off California. I tell him, "We're leaving in a few days." He says, "I'll drive by the house when I can, just a quick check." On April 19th we're rolling from Denver to Albuquerque, hopping on Amtrak to LA. We're cruising through San Bernardino, all smiles, when my phone buzzes. He's texting: "Drove by. Garage door's up like a broken window of trust. Looks like someone's inside. Waiting for the cops." I freak out. I call my wife. I am staring at the screen, no reply for 30 minutes. I am thinking, "Stolen electronics, mountain bikes, tools, truck keys—everything we parked there." My stomach drops to the floor. The Ring app shows a kid from the neighbor's place just playing with my son. Weird. It should be showing a break‑in. My wife finally remembers the prank. "Don't believe it, right?" she says. A few minutes later he texts me: "Payback is a bitch." I deserved it, honestly.
